Here in this article, we show how to use the package's function `introGraph`
to plot where the species of any plant family or genus were introduced from
and to. The graphic is a heatmap with the number of species native to each
continent (rows) that are introduced in each other continent (columns),
following the
[World Geographical Scheme for Recording Plant Distributions](https://www.tdwg.org/standards/wgsrpd/).
It helps to see which floras are the main sources of introduced plants, and
which continents receive most of them.\

\

# Setup

Install the latest development version of __expowo__ from
[GitHub](https://github.com/):

``` r
#install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("DBOSlab/expowo")
```
```{r package load, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(expowo)
```

\

# 1. Mining the species list and their distribution

`introGraph` uses as input data the species list and their native and
introduced distribution returned by `powoSpecies`. The first search downloads
the data of the World Checklist of Vascular Plants (about 90 MB) only once, so
any following search takes a few seconds.\

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fab <- powoSpecies(family = "Fabaceae",
                   verbose = FALSE)
```

\

# 2. Plotting introductions between continents

Just provide the output of `powoSpecies` to `introGraph`. Each botanical
country of the native and introduced distribution of each species is assigned
to its continent, and a species counts once for each pair of continents.
Introductions within the same continent are not shown. No download is needed,
as the continent of each botanical country is stored within __expowo__. Setting
`save = TRUE` writes the graphic within a subfolder named after the current
date, in any of the formats JPG, PDF, PNG or TIFF.\

```{r, eval = FALSE}
introGraph(inputdf = fab,
           save = TRUE,
           dir = "results_introGraph",
           filename = "intro_graph_Fabaceae",
           format = "png")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "620px", fig.cap = "FIGURE 1. Number of Fabaceae species native to each continent (rows) that are introduced in each other continent (columns)."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/intro_graph_Fabaceae.png", dpi = 300)
```

\

About 1,300 legume species are introduced in another continent. Species
native to temperate Asia, i.e. the Mediterranean and western Asian clovers,
medicks and vetches, are the most widely introduced, above all in Europe,
Africa and Northern America. Africa and tropical Asia are also major sources
of introduced legumes. The Antarctic continent of the scheme includes the
subantarctic islands, where some legumes were introduced.\

\

# 3. Plotting introductions between regions

For a finer view, the argument `level = "region"` uses the 52 regions of the
level 2 of the scheme (e.g. Brazil, Southwestern Europe, Indo-China) instead
of the nine continents. The graphic is larger, and it is saved with a larger
size accordingly.\

```{r, eval = FALSE}
introGraph(inputdf = fab,
           level = "region",
           save = TRUE,
           dir = "results_introGraph",
           filename = "intro_graph_Fabaceae_regions",
           format = "pdf")
```

\

# 4. Using the graphic object

`introGraph` returns a `ggplot` object, so the graphic can be customised with
any function of __ggplot2__. The data of the graphic has the number of species
(`species`) native to each continent or region (`from`) that are introduced in
another one (`to`).\

```{r, eval = FALSE}
p <- introGraph(fab, verbose = FALSE)

# Main routes of introduction
routes <- p$data[order(-p$data$species), c("from", "to", "species")]
head(routes)

# Adding a title
p + ggplot2::ggtitle("Where legumes were introduced")
```

\

When the input data has synonyms (a `status` column, as in
`powoSpecies(synonyms = TRUE)`), only accepted species are counted.\

\

# 5. Reference

Govaerts, R., E. Nic Lughadha, N. Black, R. Turner, and A. Paton. 2021. The
World Checklist of Vascular Plants, a continuously updated resource for
exploring global plant diversity. Scientific Data 8: 215.
